C1a.claim: antisymmetric J (2x2): x^T J x = 0 for all real x

C1a(2).claim: antisymmetric J (4x4): x^T J x = 0 for all real x

C1b.claim: (A^T M A)_ij = B(A e_i, A e_j) for general 2x2 A, M  (so A^T M A = M is form preservation)

C1c.claim: diag(2,1) keeps x^T J x = 0 yet D^T J D = 2J != J; the Hamiltonian flow exp(sK) of S9 keeps A^T J A = J

C2a.claim: symmetric M: K^T M + M K is symmetric, so conservation of z^T M z <=> K^T M + M K = 0; antisymmetric J: K = I conserves z^T J z trivially but K^T J + J K = 2J

C7a.claim: [C7-A | identity] T_k(cos φ) = cos(kφ): checked symbolically for k = 0…12, and for every k by induction: T_0 = 1, T_1(x) = x, and T_{k+1} = 2xT_k − T_{k−1} matches cos((k+1)φ) + cos((k−1)φ) = 2 cos φ cos(kφ) (symbolic in k). Hence f(x) = Σ a_k T_k(x) on [−1, 1] ⟺ F(φ) = f(cos φ) = Σ a_k cos(kφ): the Chebyshev series of f is the cosine-Fourier series of the even, 2π-periodic F, with the same coefficients

C7b.claim: [C7-A | normalization] with a_0 = (1/π)∫₀^π F(φ) dφ and a_k = (2/π)∫₀^π F(φ) cos(kφ) dφ (k ≥ 1), equivalently a_k = (2/π)∫₋₁¹ f(x)T_k(x)/√(1 − x²) dx (dx/√(1 − x²) = −dφ), the coefficients of f(x) = 1/(2 − x) are a_0 = 1/√3, a_k = (2/√3)(2 − √3)^k (both integrals agree with the closed form for k = 0…8: φ-integral error 5e-32, x-integral 2e-17, limited by the endpoint singularity of the quadrature). The complex Fourier coefficients of F are F̂(0) = a_0 and F̂(±k) = a_k/2 (k ≥ 1): the factor 2 and the halved a_0 are the only convention differences

C7c.claim: [C7-B | Fourier strip ⟺ Bernstein ellipse] x = cos(φ + iη) = cos φ cosh η − i sin φ sinh η traces the Bernstein ellipse with semi-axes cosh η, sinh η, whose sum is e^η = ρ (symbolic). So 'f analytic in E_ρ with |f| ≤ M' (Quinn, Theorem 1) is 'F(φ) = f(cos φ) analytic in the strip |Im φ| < log ρ with |F| ≤ M' (a Fourier statement). For f = 1/(2 − x) the pole x = 2 = cos(iη*) gives ρ* = e^{η*} = 2 + √3, exactly the decay ratio of C7b. Theorem 1(ii) instance at ρ = 3: M = max_(E_3)|f| = 3 = 1/(2 − 5/3), and |a_0| ≤ M, |a_k| ≤ 2Mρ^(−k) for k = 1…30

C7d.claim: [uniformity | counterexample A] f_θ(x) = cos(θx) has Chebyshev coefficients a_2m = 2(−1)^m J_2m(θ) (Jacobi–Anger; checked at θ = 5), so each member decays super-geometrically (|a_30(5)| < 1e−10). But over θ ∈ [0, 300] there is no uniform fast envelope: sup_θ |a_40(θ)| = 0.389, so a geometric envelope Cρ^(−k) would need C ≥ 0.39·ρ^40. The image at 6 sample points does not form a width hierarchy: for θ ∈ [0, 400] the point cloud has σ_6/σ_1 = 0.980, while for θ ∈ [0, 1] (where a uniform envelope exists) it is 7.8e-15. Pointwise spectral decay is not sufficient; C7 needs a family-wide envelope sup_θ |a_k(θ)| ≤ r_k

C7e.claim: [C7-B | envelope] for the family f_θ(x) = 1/(θ − x), θ ∈ [2, 3]: a_0(θ) = 1/√(θ² − 1), a_k(θ) = (2/√(θ² − 1))(θ − √(θ² − 1))^k (checked against the cosine transform at θ = 2.5); for every k = 0…11 the supremum over θ is attained at θ = 2, so the family has the uniform envelope r_k = a_k(2) = (2/√3)(2 − √3)^k (r_0 = 1/√3). The envelope is a property of the set of functions, not of any one member

C7f.claim: [C7-C | evaluation operator] at sample points x_1…x_N, the truncated part p_(m−1)(θ) = Σ_(k<m) a_k(θ)T_k evaluates as V_m a(θ) with V_ik = T_k(x_i) (exact for polynomials); the full prediction is Y(θ) = V_m a(θ) + e(θ) with every |e_i(θ)| ≤ R_m = Σ_(k≥m) r_k. For 1/(θ − x), N = 8 random points, m = 5: max |e_i| = 1.880e-03 ≤ R_5 = 2.179e-03. So Y(Θ) ⊆ V_m Q_m ⊕ [−R_m, R_m]^N, Q_m = {|a_k| ≤ r_k}

C7g.claim: [C7-C | box vs ball] coordinatewise bounds |a_k| ≤ r_k define a box; its image under V is a zonotope Z = VD·[−1, 1]^m with support function h_Z(u) = ‖DVᵀu‖₁, not an ellipsoid. Relaxing the box to the ball ‖z‖₂ ≤ √m costs the factor √m: h_Z(u) ≤ √m‖DVᵀu‖₂ = h_E(u) (2000 directions, N = m = 8), and along the first principal axis h_Z/h_E = 0.354 < 1, so the end of that axis lies in E but not in Z. Quinn's box |c̃_0| ≤ M, |c̃_j| ≤ 2M has largest norm M√(4N − 3) at a corner; the stated radius 4M√(4N − 3) is valid but loose by 4; Eq. (8) uses M√(4N − 3)

C7h.claim: [C7-C | axes] the ball of radius r maps under X to an ellipsoid with semi-axes rσ_j(X) (support function r‖Xᵀu_j‖ = rσ_j). Quinn's bound σ_j(JD) ≤ √N ρ^(−j+2)/√(ρ² − 1), j ≥ 2, holds at 12 random nodes (ρ = 2); the elementary bound σ_j(VD) ≤ ‖V‖₂ σ_j(D) holds as well. At Chebyshev nodes x_i = cos((2i − 1)π/2N), which are equally spaced in φ, discrete cosine orthogonality gives JᵀJ = diag(N, N/2, …, N/2), so the axes are EXACT: σ_1 = √N, σ_j = √(N/2)ρ^(−(j−1)) (j ≥ 2); Quinn's bound is loose there by 1.633 = √2ρ/√(ρ² − 1)

C7i.claim: [C7-C | approximation error] a uniform envelope gives sup_θ ‖f_θ − p_(m−1)(θ)‖∞ ≤ R_m = Σ_(k≥m) r_k (|T_k| ≤ 1; the Chebyshev series of a continuous f with summable coefficients converges uniformly to f). For 1/(θ − x), θ ∈ [2, 3]: the worst sup-error over θ is ≤ R_m for m = 1…10 (m = 5: 2.179e-03 ≤ 2.179e-03). For a geometric envelope r_k = 2Mρ^(−k) this is R_m = 2Mρ^(1−m)/(ρ − 1), Quinn's Theorem 1(i); here it is also below the ρ = 3, M = 3 instance of that bound

C7j.claim: [C7-C | Quinn Eq. (2), error term] exact family at N = 2 points x = ±1 (K = 2 ≤ N): f(x) = c_0 + e T_2(x) with |c_0| < r, |e| ≤ ε, so p_1 = c_0 and ‖f − p_1‖∞ = |e|. With r = 1, ε = 0.1, X = J has σ_1 = σ_2 = √2, so Eq. (2)'s hyperellipsoid is the disk of radius rσ + ε = 1.5142; the model point (c_0 + ε)(1, 1) with c_0 = 0.999 has norm 1.5542: outside. The sup-norm error is a box [−ε, ε]^N (Euclidean radius √N ε), and an ellipsoid ⊕ box is not the ellipsoid with additively enlarged axes. Valid replacements: (1) extent along the j-th axis u_j of H_P ≤ 2rσ_j + 2ε‖u_j‖₁ (≤ 2rσ_j + 2√N ε): equality is attained here; (2) Y ⊆ the ellipsoid with semi-axes √2·√(r²σ_j² + Nε²) (support functions; 20000 random family points inside)

C7k.claim: [C7-C | reparametrization] the hypotheses (a uniform envelope over the SET {f_θ}) and the enclosure (V, D, R_m) do not involve θ-coordinates: for 1/(θ − x) charted by θ ∈ [2, 3] or by θ = 2 + φ³, φ ∈ [0, 1], the envelopes agree to 1e−14 for k = 0…9, so W_j^bound is unchanged. The Fisher metric at the same point is not: g_φ/g_θ = (dθ/dφ)² = 0.5625 at φ = 0.5. The enclosure is a prediction-space object; Fisher eigenvalues are chart-dependent (MMIb)

C7l.claim: [metric dependence | counterexample B] the same envelope and sample points under the prediction metric W = diag(1, …, 1, 10⁶): σ_1 grows by 402× and the ratio σ_2/σ_1 moves from 3.789e-01 to 1.438e-03: the apparent hierarchy changes. What survives is the upper bound σ_j(W^(1/2)VD) ≤ ‖W^(1/2)V‖₂ r_(j): the envelope's rate with a metric-dependent constant. Widths are prediction-metric dependent

C7m.claim: [sampling dependence | counterexample C] with NO coefficient decay (r_k ≡ 1), the evaluation matrix alone decides: at 10 Chebyshev nodes σ_10/σ_1 = 1/√2 (no hierarchy), at 10 points clustered in [0.9, 1] σ_10/σ_1 = 8.6e-18. Finite-N prediction-space axes depend strongly on where the model is sampled

C7n.claim: [direction of implication] a uniform envelope is SUFFICIENT for the enclosure bound; it is not necessary for a width hierarchy. (1) f_θ = θT_20(x), θ ∈ [0, 1]: the image at 25 Chebyshev nodes is a segment (one nonzero width, σ_2/σ_1 < 1e−12), yet the envelope is r_20 = 1 and 0 elsewhere: hierarchy with no coefficient decay. (2) C7m: clustered sampling produces a hierarchy from a flat envelope. Hierarchies can arise for reasons unrelated to Fourier / Chebyshev smoothness

C7o.claim: [upper bound only | counterexample E] f_θ(x) = θ|x|, θ ∈ [0, 1]: the coefficients of |x| decay only like k^(−2) (a_0 = 2/π, a_2m = (−1)^(m+1)·4/(π(4m² − 1))), so the enclosure's axes decay slowly (σ_2/σ_1 = 0.471 for VD at 16 Chebyshev nodes); the actual image is a segment (σ_2/σ_1 < 1e−12). Weak spectral decay does not imply a wide image: the bound is an upper bound, not the width spectrum

C7p.claim: [enclosure ≠ manifold width | counterexample F] a_k(θ) = (θ/ρ)^k, θ ∈ [−1, 1], ρ = 2, i.e. f_θ(x) = (1 − (θ/ρ)x)/(1 − 2(θ/ρ)x + (θ/ρ)²) (Chebyshev generating function; checked at θ = 0.7): strong decay, but the coefficients are correlated and fill only a curve inside the envelope box. At 10 Chebyshev nodes, the image's extent along each axis of the enclosure is below the bound (zonotope + 2R_m‖u‖₁ error term) for all 10 axes, but along axis 3 it is only 0.495 of it. The image is a 1-parameter curve whose own point-cloud spectrum decays faster than the enclosure's axis ratios (j = 6: σ_6/σ_1 = 1.0e-03 for the curve vs 2.2e-02 for the enclosure)

C7q.claim: [actual width vs W_j^bound] for 1/(θ − x), θ ∈ [2, 3], at 8 Chebyshev nodes: along every principal axis u_j of the enclosure, the actual extent of the model image E_j = sup_(θ,θ′) u_j·(Y(θ) − Y(θ′)) is ≤ W_j^bound = 2h_Z(u_j) + 2R_m‖u_j‖₁ on all 8 axes, with E_j/W_j^bound between 0.19 and 0.45: the bound overestimates by 2× or more on every axis. The image is close to a curve (point-cloud σ_2/σ_1 = 0.028, σ_3/σ_1 = 7.8e-04). Three objects stay distinct: the actual image's extents, the enclosing set, and the bound on its widths

C7r.claim: [direct periodic route] for 2π-periodic f_θ(t) = Σ f̂_θ(k)e^(ikt) with |f̂_θ(k)| ≤ r_|k| uniformly, at N equally spaced samples the Fourier evaluation matrix has orthogonal columns (FᴴF = N·I for 2K + 1 ≤ N), so the ellipsoid axes are EXACTLY √N × the sorted envelope (each r_k twice, for ±k). At non-uniform samples only σ_j(FD) ≤ ‖F‖₂ r_(j) holds, without equality. Modes |k| ≥ N alias onto lower ones (e^(i(k+N)t_j) = e^(ikt_j)), so the tail must be counted as error. This is discrete Fourier orthogonality plus a singular-value inequality: elementary, not a new theorem

C7s.claim: [function space; N-dependence] the uniform envelope gives an N-independent statement: every f_θ lies within sup-norm distance R_m of the m-dimensional polynomial space Π_(m−1), so the Kolmogorov m-width d_m({f_θ}; C[−1, 1]) ≤ R_m. At N samples (Euclidean) the distance of Y(θ) to range(V_m) is ≤ √N·R_m; in the RMS metric ‖·‖₂/√N it is ≤ R_m for every N (1/(θ − x), m = 5: 1.17e-03, 1.17e-03, 1.17e-03 ≤ R_5 = 2.18e-03 at N = 8, 32, 128). A finite-N bound with a √N factor is not, by itself, an infinite-dimensional theorem; the function-space statement is the N-free one

C7t.claim: [the project's model F-C] y_θ(t) = e^(−θ₁t) + e^(−θ₂t), t ∈ [0, 1] (x = 2t − 1), θ ∈ [0, 4]² (a bounded domain is needed for a uniform envelope): the coefficients of e^(−s(x+1)) are e^(−s)I_0(s) and 2(−1)^k e^(−s)I_k(s) (checked), the uniform envelope r_k = 2·sup_s |…| decays super-geometrically (r_10/r_1 = 1.9e-07), and at 8 Chebyshev nodes the extent of the F-C image along every axis of the enclosure is below W_j^bound (all 8 axes; e.g. axis 2: 1.753e+00 ≤ 3.506e+00). The enclosure is the same for θ or log θ charts (C7k), unlike the Fisher eigenvalues (MMIb)

C7u.claim: [C7 verdict] principal status C7-KNOWN-REFORMULATION. The chain holds as a SUFFICIENT, UPPER-BOUND, restricted statement: cosine-Fourier coefficients of F_θ(φ) = f_θ(cos φ) are the Chebyshev coefficients of f_θ (exact; C7a, C7b); strip analyticity of F_θ is Bernstein-ellipse analyticity of f_θ (C7c); a FAMILY-WIDE envelope r_k ≥ sup_θ |a_k(θ)| (C7d, C7e) bounds the truncation error by R_m (C7i) and encloses Y(Θ) ⊆ ℝᴺ in V_m D_m·[−1, 1]^m ⊕ [−R_m, R_m]^N, whose widths are bounded by r_k and the evaluation operator (C7f–C7h, C7s), independently of the parameterization (C7k). Every ingredient is Quinn et al. 2019 plus standard approximation theory after x = cos φ. It is not necessary (C7n), not exact (C7o–C7q), metric- and sampling-dependent (C7l, C7m), and Quinn's Eq. (2) error term needs the correction of C7j

C7La.claim: [published Eq. (2), formalized] Eq. (2) of the published PRL ('we can define a hyperellipsoid HY that must enclose model manifold Y, where the cross-sectional widths are given by ℓj(HY) = 2rσj(X) + 2‖y − pN−1‖∞') is tested as: Y ⊆ H_Y, the ellipsoid with the principal axes of H_P = X·{‖b‖₂ ≤ r} and semi-axes rσ_j(X) + ε, ε = sup_θ ‖y_θ − p_(N−1)(θ)‖∞. Check of the formalization: at ε = 0 it is H_P of Eq. (1), whose boundary X·b (‖b‖ = r) is attained; for X = [[1, −1], [1, 1]] (T_0, T_1 at t = ±1) σ_1 = σ_2 = √2 exactly

C7Lb.claim: [error box] if ‖y − p‖∞ ≤ ε on [−1, 1], the sampled error vector lies in the box [−ε, ε]^N, not in a Euclidean ball of radius ε. For a Euclidean unit u: sup_(e ∈ [−ε, ε]^N) uᵀe = Σ|u_i|ε = ε‖u‖₁, attained at e = ε·sign(u) (linear function on a box: maximum at a vertex; checked against all 2^N vertices for 200 random u, N = 2…6). Hence the error adds up to 2ε‖u‖₁ to the width along u, with 1 ≤ ‖u‖₁ ≤ √N (Cauchy–Schwarz; equality at u = e_1 and at u = (1, …, 1)/√N)

C7Lc.claim: [Eq. (2): exact counterexamples, Euclidean prediction space] (i) N = 2, t = (−1, 1), Chebyshev basis: y_θ(t) = θ₁ + θ₂T₂(t), |θ₁| < r = 1, |θ₂| ≤ ε = 1/10; then p₁ = θ₁ (b = (θ₁, 0), ‖b‖₂ < r) and ‖y − p₁‖∞ = |θ₂| ≤ ε. X = [[1, −1], [1, 1]], σ₁ = σ₂ = √2, so Eq. (2) gives the disk of radius √2 + 1/10; the model point at θ = (99/100, 1/10) is Y = (109/100)(1, 1) with ‖Y‖² − (√2 + 1/10)² = 0.0834 > 0 (exact): outside. Along u = (1, 1)/√2 the family's width is 2.2√2 = 3.1113 > 2√2 + 1/5 = 3.0284, equal to the corrected 2rσ + 2ε‖u‖₁. (ii) Distinct singular values: t = (−1, 0, 1), y_θ = θ_a(T₀ + T₂)/√2 + θ_eT₄ (T₄ = 1 at all three points), X has σ = (2, √2, √2) with first axis u₁ = (1, 0, 1)/√2; at θ = (99/100, 1/10) the Eq. (2) ellipsoid value is 1.0249 > 1. Counterexample to Eq. (2) as written under the ordinary Euclidean prediction-space interpretation

C7Ld.claim: [directional width ≠ containment] a bound on the widths of a set along chosen axes does not give an enclosing ellipsoid with those widths. Even with a Euclidean-ball error (the most favourable reading), E ⊕ δB₂ has width exactly 2(a_j + δ) along each axis of E (support functions add), yet it is not contained in the ellipsoid with semi-axes a_j + δ: for a = (1, 1/10), δ = 1/10 the point of E at angle π/4 moved by δ along its normal gives 1.1493 > 1. Three objects are kept apart: the exact Minkowski set H_P ⊕ [−ε, ε]^N, the directional support-function bound h(u) = h_(H_P)(u) + ε‖u‖₁, and an enclosing-ellipsoid relaxation (C7Le)

C7Le.claim: [conservative ellipsoid, PROVED] for H_P = {Az : ‖z‖₂ ≤ 1} and δ > 0: H_P ⊕ B₂(δ) ⊆ E(Q) = {x : xᵀQ⁻¹x ≤ 1} with Q = 2(AAᵀ + δ²I). Proof: support functions h_(H_P)(u) = ‖Aᵀu‖, h_(B₂(δ))(u) = δ, h_(E(Q))(u) = √(uᵀQu) = √2·√(‖Aᵀu‖² + δ²) ≥ ‖Aᵀu‖ + δ because 2(α² + β²) − (α + β)² = (α − β)² ≥ 0; compact convex sets satisfy K ⊆ L ⟺ h_K ≤ h_L. Since [−ε, ε]^N ⊆ B₂(√N ε), H_P ⊕ [−ε, ε]^N ⊆ E(2(AAᵀ + Nε²I)), whose semi-axes are √2·√(s_j(A)² + Nε²) (s_j padded with zeros to N): checked on 60 random (A, ε) with 300 points each, box corners included. The factor √2 cannot be dropped in general: for a segment plus a ball, the point (1 + δ, 0) lies outside E(AAᵀ + δ²I)

C7Lf.claim: [coefficient radius] from |c_0| ≤ M, |c_j| ≤ 2Mρ^(−j) and c̃_j = ρ^j c_j: |c̃_0| ≤ M, |c̃_j| ≤ 2M, so ‖c̃‖₂² ≤ M² + 4M²(N − 1) = M²(4N − 3) (symbolic; equality at a corner of the box), i.e. ‖c̃‖₂ ≤ M√(4N − 3). The printed '‖c̃‖₂ < 4M√(4N − 3)' is valid but loose by exactly 4, and the printed diameter 'ℓj(HP) = 8M√(4N − 3)σj(X)' is 2rσ_j with that loose radius

C7Lg.claim: [Eq. (8) constants] Eq. (8)'s first term 2M√(4N² − 3N)ρ^(−j+2)/√(ρ² − 1) equals 2·M√(4N − 3)·(√Nρ^(−j+2)/√(ρ² − 1)) (√(4N² − 3N) = √N√(4N − 3), symbolic): it uses the TIGHT radius M√(4N − 3), not the printed 4M√(4N − 3), which would give 4× Eq. (8). Internal constant inconsistency, likely a typographical factor; not a new mathematical result. The second term 4Mρ^(−N+1)/(ρ − 1) is 2ε with ε from Theorem 1(i): the additive error term of Eq. (2), which as a directional width along u_j needs 2ε‖u_j‖₁ (≤ 2√N ε) and as an enclosing ellipsoid needs C7Le

C7Lh.claim: [Fourier / Chebyshev analyticity, exact form] with z = e^(iφ), φ = α + iβ: |z| = e^(−β), so the annulus ρ^(−1) < |z| < ρ is the strip |Im φ| < log ρ. The Joukowski map x = (z + z^(−1))/2 = cos φ folds z ↔ 1/z (2-to-1), sends |z| = s and |z| = 1/s onto the same ellipse with semi-axes (s ± 1/s)/2 (checked at s = 2) and |z| = 1 onto [−1, 1] twice; T_k((z + z^(−1))/2) = (z^k + z^(−k))/2 (k ≤ 8). Exact statement: f is analytic in the open region bounded by E_ρ with |f| ≤ M ⟺ F = f∘cos is analytic in |Im φ| < log ρ with |F| ≤ M; such an F is automatically 2π-periodic and EVEN. Conversely an analytic, 2π-periodic, even F on the strip descends to such an f (G(z) = F has a Laurent series with g_(−k) = g_k, so G = g_0 + 2Σ g_k T_k(x)); without evenness it need not (sin φ is entire and periodic but odd). Example: 1/(2 − x) gives G with poles z = 2 ∓ √3, i.e. exactly the annulus with ρ = 2 + √3

C7Li.claim: [node convention] the exact-axes statement holds for Gauss–Chebyshev (first-kind) nodes x_i = cos((i + 1/2)π/N), i = 0, …, N − 1 (the same set as cos((2i − 1)π/2N), i = 1, …, N): with the unweighted Euclidean metric, Σ_i T_j(x_i)T_k(x_i) = 0 (j ≠ k), N/2 (j = k ≥ 1), N (j = k = 0) for j, k ≤ N − 1 (N = 7, 50-digit check), so σ(V D) = {√N r_0} ∪ {√(N/2) r_k}. It FAILS for Chebyshev–Lobatto (extrema) nodes cos(iπ/(N − 1)) with the unweighted metric: Σ_i T_0T_2(x_i) = 1 ≠ 0; there, orthogonality needs the weights (1/2, 1, …, 1, 1/2), with norms N − 1 (k = 0, N − 1) and (N − 1)/2 otherwise

C7Lj.claim: [periodic convention] N equally spaced samples t_j = 2πj/N (N = 12). Complex basis e^(ikt), |k| ≤ K, with an envelope on the complex coefficients |f̂(k)| ≤ r_|k|: FᴴF = N·I exactly when the 2K + 1 frequencies are distinct mod N (2K + 1 ≤ N), and then σ(FD) = √N·r_|k|, each r_k (k ≥ 1) twice (±k). Real basis 1, cos kt, sin kt with |a_k|, |b_k| ≤ r_k: Gram diag(N, N/2, …), so σ = √N r_0 and √(N/2) r_k (twice). Nyquist mode (N even, k = N/2): e^(±iNt/2) coincide and sin(Nt/2) vanishes on the samples, so it is excluded by 2K + 1 ≤ N. Modes alias: e^(i(k+N)t_j) = e^(ikt_j). 'Exactly √N × the envelope' holds only in the complex convention with 2K + 1 ≤ N

C7Lk.claim: [Kolmogorov width] d_m(F; C[−1, 1]) = inf over subspaces L with dim L = m of sup_(f ∈ F) inf_(g ∈ L) ‖f − g‖∞. Choose L_m = span{T_0, …, T_(m−1)} (dimension m: degrees 0…m − 1) and g = Σ_(k<m) a_k(f)T_k: ‖f − g‖∞ ≤ Σ_(k≥m)|a_k(f)| ≤ Σ_(k≥m) r_k = R_m, so d_m ≤ R_m. Indexing checked on 1/(θ − x), θ ∈ [2, 3], m = 1…8: dim L_m = m, the truncation error is ≤ R_m, and at θ = 2, x = 1 (all a_k > 0, T_k(1) = 1) it EQUALS R_m, so this choice of L_m cannot give R_(m+1). This is a function-space width (sup norm, N-free), not an axis of the finite prediction-space hyperellipsoid

C7Ll.claim: [no lower bound from an envelope alone] the envelope is an UPPER constraint |a_k(θ)| ≤ r_k: any family occupying a subset of the allowed coefficient region satisfies it. For the 1/(θ − x) envelope (r_0 = 1/√3) and every η > 0 (η = 1, 1e−3, 1e−9 checked), the family f_θ = θ·(η/2√N)·T_0, θ ∈ [0, 1], satisfies the envelope, its image at N = 8 nodes has diameter < η and all widths beyond the first are 0; the singleton {0} satisfies it with all widths 0. Z3c.claim: shifting every mass by the same step a moves the balancing point by a: R_CM(r + a) = R_CM(r) + a

Z3d.claim: with u_i = m_i (r_i - R_CM), sum u_i = 0 exactly; and for m_i > 0, u_i = 0 only when r_i = R_CM, so the contributions are nonzero unless a mass sits at R_CM

Z5a.claim: boundary: F(x) = |x|^2 on R^2 is 0 only at x = 0 (n^2 + a^2 > 0 and a^2 + n^2 > 0 for real n != 0), so a zero reading can determine the state for some measurements
